title: Muesli bowl
baby: For baby, offer soft banana or curd separately. Avoid whole nuts.
recipe: Add muesli to milk or curd. Top with banana or apple. Keep nuts optional and chopped for adults.

title: Sooji idli
baby: Soft idli can be mashed with ghee, curd, or mild sambar. Keep baby portion low salt.
recipe: Mix sooji, curd, water and salt. Rest briefly. Add Eno before steaming. Steam in idli moulds and serve with chutney.

title: Besan cabbage chilla
baby: Make a small soft chilla with minimal salt and no chilli. Cut into tiny pieces if baby is ready for finger foods.
recipe: Mix besan with shredded cabbage, coriander, water and mild spices. Cook chillas on a tawa. Serve with curd or chutney.

title: Aloo paratha + curd
baby: Offer soft paratha pieces with curd if baby can chew. Keep spices very mild.
recipe: Stuff wheat dough with mashed spiced potato. Roll and cook with ghee. Serve with curd.

title: Gobi paratha + curd
baby: Offer soft outer paratha pieces or very mild filling only if cauliflower suits baby.
recipe: Grate cauliflower, squeeze excess water, season mildly and stuff into dough. Cook parathas and serve with curd.

title: Poha
baby: For baby, keep aside soft poha before chilli. Mash with curd if needed.
recipe: Rinse poha and keep aside. Temper mustard, curry leaves, onion and peas. Add turmeric and poha. Finish with lemon.

title: Dosa
baby: Soft dosa pieces with ghee or curd can work. Avoid crispy hard pieces for baby.
recipe: Spread dosa batter on a hot tawa. Cook with a little ghee. Serve plain or with potato, chutney, or sambar.

title: Spiced sautéed idli
baby: Keep a few plain soft idli pieces aside before sautéing.
recipe: Cut idlis into pieces. Sauté with curry leaves, onion, capsicum and mild spices. Finish with chutney powder if desired.

title: Bread peanut butter banana
baby: Offer banana separately. Peanut butter only if already introduced and spread very thinly.
recipe: Toast bread if you like. Spread peanut butter, add banana slices, and serve open or as a sandwich.

title: Oats pancake
baby: Make small soft pancakes with banana and oats. Avoid honey for baby under 1 year.
recipe: Blend oats, banana and milk into a batter. Cook small pancakes on a tawa with ghee. Serve with fruit.

title: Avocado cheese sandwich
baby: Offer soft avocado separately if already introduced. Avoid hard toasted pieces for baby.
recipe: Mash avocado with a little salt and lemon for adults. Layer with cheese in bread and toast lightly or serve fresh.

title: Dal makhni
baby: Too heavy/spiced for baby. Offer plain dal rice or curd rice separately.
recipe: Pressure cook soaked urad dal until soft. Simmer with tomato, ginger-garlic and mild spices. Finish with butter or cream.

title: Rajma
baby: Rajma may be heavy. Offer soft rice, curd, or a tiny mashed portion only if already introduced.
recipe: Pressure cook soaked rajma. Simmer with onion-tomato masala. Serve with rice and curd.

title: Chhole
baby: Keep baby meal separate. Chhole can be heavy and spicy.
recipe: Pressure cook soaked chana. Simmer with onion-tomato masala and chhole masala. Serve with rice or roti.

title: Kadhi chawal
baby: Baby can have soft rice with plain curd or a mild kadhi portion if tolerated.
recipe: Whisk curd, besan and water. Simmer with turmeric and tempering. Serve with steamed rice.

title: Mixed dal
baby: Good baby option if cooked soft and kept low spice before tadka.
recipe: Pressure cook mixed dals with turmeric and tomato. Add simple tadka for adults. Serve with rice or roti.

title: Pasta
baby: Use soft pasta pieces with mild sauce and less salt.
recipe: Boil pasta. Make a tomato-garlic vegetable sauce. Toss pasta and finish with cheese.

title: Veg pulao + raita
baby: Keep a soft, less-spiced portion aside. Mash with curd.
recipe: Cook rice with mixed vegetables and mild spices. Serve with cucumber raita.

title: Matar paneer
baby: Offer soft paneer cubes separately if tolerated. Avoid spicy gravy.
recipe: Make onion-tomato gravy, add peas and paneer. Simmer gently. Serve with roti or rice.

title: Palak paneer
baby: Keep a mild palak puree aside if baby has had spinach before. Paneer can be offered soft.
recipe: Blanch palak and blend. Cook with mild masala, add paneer and simmer. Serve with roti.

title: Palak corn koftas
baby: Not ideal as-is for baby. Offer plain soft palak/paneer separately.
recipe: Make soft koftas with corn, paneer or potato. Prepare palak gravy and simmer koftas briefly before serving.

title: Aloo beet paneer koftas
baby: Offer plain beet, potato or paneer mash separately before masala.
recipe: Make koftas using mashed potato, grated beet and paneer. Add to a mild onion-tomato gravy.

title: Tofu manchurian
baby: Not suitable as-is because of sauces. Offer plain tofu separately if introduced.
recipe: Pan-toss tofu cubes. Make garlic-capsicum sauce with soy and cornflour slurry. Toss tofu and serve with rice or noodles.

title: Bhindi stuffed
baby: Bhindi texture may be tricky. Offer a separate soft vegetable or dal rice.
recipe: Slit bhindi and fill with dry masala. Cook covered on low flame until tender. Serve with roti.

title: Bhindi bhujiya
baby: Offer only if baby handles texture; otherwise keep dal/curd rice for baby.
recipe: Slice bhindi and sauté with mild spices until non-sticky and cooked. Serve with roti and curd.

title: Methi mooli paratha
baby: Offer soft pieces with curd if baby can chew and has tolerated these ingredients.
recipe: Mix chopped methi and squeezed grated mooli into atta with mild spices. Roll parathas and cook with ghee.

title: Black chana
baby: Can be heavy. Offer dal rice, curd rice, or a tiny mashed portion only if already introduced.
recipe: Pressure cook soaked black chana. Cook with onion-tomato masala or keep it dry-style. Serve with rice or roti.

title: Sprouts sautéed
baby: Avoid whole sprouts for baby. Offer a separate soft meal.
recipe: Steam or sauté sprouts with mild spices. Finish with lemon and coriander. Pair with roti, curd or rice.

title: Bhindi bhujiya
baby: Offer only if baby handles texture; otherwise keep dal/curd rice for baby.
recipe: Slice bhindi and sauté with mild spices until non-sticky and cooked. Serve with roti and curd.

title: Bhindi stuffed
baby: Bhindi texture may be tricky. Offer a separate soft vegetable or dal rice.
recipe: Slit bhindi and fill with dry masala. Cook covered on low flame until tender. Serve with roti.

title: Mushroom sandwich
baby: Mushrooms can be chewy. Offer soft bread/cheese or a separate baby meal.
recipe: Sauté mushrooms with garlic and butter. Fill bread with mushroom mix and cheese. Toast lightly.

title: Veg cutlet burger
baby: Offer deconstructed soft potato/veg cutlet pieces separately.
recipe: Make potato-mixed veg cutlets. Toast buns and assemble with cheese, tomato and a curd-based sauce.

title: Gobi sabji
baby: Offer soft cauliflower only if tolerated and cooked very soft.
recipe: Cook cauliflower with mild spices and optional potato. Serve with roti and curd.

title: Paneer bhurji + roti
baby: Offer soft paneer crumbs separately if tolerated. Keep spices mild.
recipe: Sauté onion, tomato and capsicum. Add crumbled paneer, turmeric, mild masala and coriander. Serve with roti.

title: Paneer kofta curry
baby: Offer plain soft paneer/potato separately before masala.
recipe: Make paneer koftas and prepare onion-tomato gravy. Add koftas just before serving.

title: Pasta - spinach
baby: Use soft pasta and mild spinach sauce with less salt if baby has had spinach.
recipe: Boil pasta. Make a spinach-garlic sauce with milk or cheese. Toss pasta and serve warm.

title: Beans bhujiya
baby: Cook beans very soft or offer a separate baby meal depending on chewing ability.
recipe: Chop beans finely and sauté with mild spices. Add potato if needed. Serve with roti.

title: Veg kofta curry
baby: Offer soft boiled vegetables separately before masala.
recipe: Make koftas using mashed vegetables and potato. Simmer in onion-tomato gravy and serve with roti.

title: Chana dal
baby: Can be slightly heavy. Offer well-cooked mashed dal only if already introduced.
recipe: Pressure cook chana dal until soft but not mushy. Add mild tadka and serve with rice or roti.

title: Mixed dal
baby: Good baby option if cooked soft and kept low spice before tadka.
recipe: Pressure cook mixed dals with turmeric and tomato. Add simple tadka for adults. Serve with rice or roti.

title: Dal makhni
baby: Too heavy/spiced for baby. Offer plain dal rice or curd rice separately.
recipe: Pressure cook soaked urad dal until soft. Simmer with tomato, ginger-garlic and mild spices. Finish with butter or cream.

title: Palak corn sandwich
baby: Offer soft palak/corn filling only if texture is safe; avoid hard toast pieces.
recipe: Sauté palak and corn with garlic. Mix with cheese. Fill bread and toast lightly.

title: Beet aloo tofu sandwich
baby: Offer plain beet-potato mash or soft tofu separately if already introduced.
recipe: Make a beet, potato and tofu filling. Add mild seasoning, spread in bread and toast or grill.

title: Samosa
baby: Not suitable for baby as-is. Offer fruit, curd, or soft homemade snack separately.
recipe: Heat ready/frozen samosas as per packet or home method. Serve with green chutney and tea.

title: Dhokla
baby: Soft dhokla can be offered in tiny pieces if low salt and no chilli.
recipe: Prepare batter, add Eno, steam until soft. Temper lightly with mustard and curry leaves.

title: Pani puri
baby: Not for baby. Keep a separate baby snack.
recipe: Prepare potato filling, mint water and sweet chutney. Assemble fresh while eating.

title: Bread pakora
baby: Not suitable for baby as-is. Offer plain bread/banana/curd separately.
recipe: Make besan batter. Stuff bread with potato if desired, dip and fry or shallow-fry. Serve with chutney.

title: Makhana + fruit + milk
baby: Use age-safe fruit pieces or mashed fruit. Avoid whole makhana for baby unless powdered/softened.
recipe: Roast makhana with ghee. Serve with fruit and milk. Add mild seasoning for adults.
